We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced and qualified Panel Beater to join either our AMA Group Solutions or Capital S.M.A.R.T Repairs team to undertake quality workmanship to ensure vehicles are returned to their pre-accident condition. Check received parts are correct and for defects

Label and store parts

Reassemble vehicle

Coach apprentices when required

Advertisement – Clinical Support Worker

Location: Mascot 2020
Salary: $78,000 – $85,000 per annum (excluding superannuation)
Job Type: Full-time

Just Better Care Eastern Suburbs is looking for passionate Clinical Support Worker to join our caring and dynamic team.

We provide in-home disability and aged care services, supporting people to live independently and with dignity. We believe that people of all ages and abilities deserve access to the support and resources they need to live where and how they choose.

Our office services four key areas in the Sydney Metro region: Eastern Suburbs, Inner West, Sutherland, and St George.

About the Role

This role involves working directly with customers, supporting them in various aspects of daily living while respecting their independence, dignity, and safety. You will be providing assistance to customers with physical, mental, emotional, and social disabilities in their homes and communities.

Main Duties:

- Assisting clients with their personal care needs such as showering, dressing and eating.
- Assisting clients with their mobility and communication needs.
- Participating in planning the care of individuals.
- Following therapy plans such as interventions to assist those with dementia and behavioural problems.
- Observing and reporting changes in client’s condition, and reporting complaints about care.
- Assisting with rehabilitation exercises, basic treatment and delivering medications.
- Providing direct support and assistance to therapists.
- The Clinical Support Worker provides and delivers individual and personalised support and resources to customers, so that they may continue to live in their homes.
- The Clinical Support Worker responsibilities may include, working under the guidance and supervision of medical professionals, monitoring and communicating customer’s condition to the Coordinator, transportation, light domestic duties, personal hygiene, providing meals and other health and wellness related activities.
- The Clinical Support Workers will demonstrate a commitment to best practice, ensuring that all services are provided in a caring and respectful way in accordance with Just Better Care’s policy and procedures.

Essential Requirements:

Essential

- AQF Certificate II or III (ANZSCO Skill Level 4)
- At least one year of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications listed above. In some instances relevant experience and/or on-the-job training may be required in addition to the formal qualification.
- Experience in high care such as spinal cord injury, palliative care, mental health support, catheter care, or epilepsy/seizure management.
- Previous experience with manual handling and various types of assistive equipment.
- Registration or licensing may be required.
- NDIS Worker Screening Clearance / Criminal Record Check
- Current First Aid certificate/CPR
- Current Australian Drivers Licence
- Reliable, registered, and insured vehicle
- Smartphone with internet access
- Proof of Working Rights in Australia (i.e. Birth Certificate/Citizenship Certificate/Passport/VISA)
- Ability to be reliably contacted via telephone and email
- Experience or willingness to assist with personal care and daily living tasks
- Reliable, punctual, and efficient in completing duties
- Respectful, client-focused attitude with a commitment to quality care
- Team-oriented with good communication and interpersonal skills
- Willingness to learn, develop skills, and participate in ongoing training
- Good written and spoken English skills for effective workplace communication

Desirable

- Current Working with Children Check (where required in accordance with state based legislation)

Why Join Just Better Care

- Be part of a close-knit, friendly, and supportive team
- Career development and ongoing training opportunities
- Strong internal support network – we care about your success
- Competitive salary and benefits
- Access to our Employee Assistance Program

Quality Australian manufacturing is in our DNA. We have been manufacturing boots, accessories and hardwearing apparel in Adelaide since our inception in 1932.

Position Summary
We are seeking Full-Time employees to join our Apparel & Craft Team at our Workshop in Salisbury, Adelaide. As part of our Apparel & Craft department, you will be responsible for supporting our production lines in producing quality clothing/craft product and gaining an understanding of our products and processes.

We are looking for individuals who are enthusiastic, task orientated and reliable. You will need to be good with your hands, ready to learn and have a good attitude to work.

Key Responsibilities
Consistently achieve production KPIs while maintaining high-quality standards.
Collaborate effectively with team members to meet production goals.
Adhere to all safe work procedures and ensure compliance with workplace safety standards.
Maintain a clean and organized working environment, including performing general housekeeping duties.
Operate an automatic cutting machine efficiently and safely.
Monitor the quality of fabric and cutting work, promptly addressing any issues.

Skills and Experience
Prior experience operating sewing machines is essential.
Familiarity with production or manufacturing environments is highly desirable.
Ability to work effectively in a team and follow reasonable directions.
Exceptional attention to detail, coupled with a strong work ethic.
Reliable, punctual, and flexible, with the willingness to work overtime as needed.

What We Offer
Long-term career opportunities
On-the-job training
40% employee discount
Discount private health insurance
Paid Parental Leave
On-site canteen
Employee rewards and benefits
As part of the selection process, applicants must be prepared to undergo a pre-employment medical examination, including functional, audiometric, vision, drug, and alcohol testing.

About Us
Since 1932, we have answered a call for hardwearing, timeless products that can hold up against the harsh conditions of the Australian outback - and look good whilst doing it. Our bestselling leather boots and belts are still crafted by hand in Adelaide, South Australia, alongside an ever-growing range of apparel, accessories and lifestyle products. At the heart of everything we do is a simple promise of loyalty and endurance; a commitment that our products will accompany their wearer on all of life’s great journeys. Reginald Murray ‘RM’ Williams always said, ‘it’s the people who make a company’ and we stand by that statement today, with a global network of teams that feels like family. A culture of growth, development and team spirit is central to our success. 
 
Appreciates the importance and value of a diverse workforce and is committed to the principle of equal opportunity for all employees and to provide employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions is based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, colour, religion or belief, sex, gender identity, national origin or family or parental status. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

Please note, only applicants with the legal right work in Australia will be considered for this role.

Welder/Fabricator – Multiple Permanent Opportunities

Perth, Western Australia | Full-Time | Sponsorship Available

MYAC Resources is seeking experienced Welder/Fabricators to join our growing network of leading employers across Perth, Western Australia.

We have multiple long-term opportunities available for skilled tradespeople who take pride in producing high-quality work and want to build a secure and rewarding career with established Australian businesses.

Whether you are already living in Australia or looking to relocate from overseas, employer sponsorship may be available for suitably qualified candidates.

About the Role

As a Welder/Fabricator, you will be involved in the fabrication, assembly and repair of metal components across a range of manufacturing, engineering and industrial projects.

Working in modern, well-equipped workshops, you will be part of a professional team committed to quality workmanship and high safety standards.

Your responsibilities may include:

Manufacturing components and welded assemblies from engineering drawings.
Completing precision fabrication and welding work in accordance with quality requirements.
Working with mechanical and engineering teams to manufacture high-quality products.
Identifying repair requirements and estimating repair times.
Operating fabrication machinery and workshop equipment.
Inspecting completed work to ensure it meets the required standards.
Maintaining a clean, organised and safe work area.
About You

To be successful, you will have:

Certificate III in Engineering – Fabrication Trade, including MEM30305, MEM31922, MEM30319 or MEM31925, or an equivalent recognised qualification.
A minimum of three to five years’ experience as a Welder/Fabricator or Boilermaker.
Proficiency in FCAW, GMAW and CAC-A (Air Carbon Arc Cutting).
The ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and fabrication plans.
The ability to complete welding qualification tests to AS/NZS 1554 SP requirements.
Experience operating fabrication machinery and workshop equipment.
Strong fabrication, measuring and welding skills.
High attention to detail and pride in producing quality workmanship.
The ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Good communication and problem-solving skills.
A strong commitment to workplace safety and quality standards.
A reliable attitude and strong work ethic.
The ability to complete a pre-employment medical, drug and alcohol screening, and other required employment checks.
Highly Regarded
Forklift Licence (LF).
Current Australian C Class Driver’s Licence.
Dogging (DG), Basic Rigging (RB) or EWP High Risk Work Licence.
Previous experience within heavy fabrication, mining, manufacturing or industrial environments.
What’s on Offer
Permanent, full-time employment.
Multiple opportunities across Perth, Western Australia.
Competitive salary packages with overtime opportunities.
Long-term career stability with established Australian employers.
Modern workshop facilities and quality equipment.
Ongoing training and career development.
Supportive and safety-focused team environments.
Employer sponsorship opportunities for eligible candidates.
Support for suitably qualified overseas applicants planning to relocate to Australia.
Employer Sponsorship

MYAC Resources has extensive experience connecting skilled tradespeople with genuine, long-term employment opportunities across Australia.

Employer sponsorship may be available for suitably qualified candidates, subject to employer approval, skills assessment requirements and Australian migration eligibility.

Why Join MYAC Resources?

MYAC Resources specialises in connecting skilled tradespeople with leading employers across Australia’s manufacturing, engineering, mining and industrial sectors.

We don’t just recruit people—we help build long-term careers. From your initial application through to placement and ongoing support, our recruitment team is committed to helping you succeed.

Apply Now

If you are an experienced Welder/Fabricator looking for your next opportunity in Perth, we would like to hear from you.

Submit your application using the Apply Now button or email your current resume to recruitment@myacresources.com.au.

One of our recruitment specialists will contact shortlisted applicants to discuss available opportunities.

Steamatic is Australia’s longest established and largest restoration Company with over 35 locations throughout Australia and growing each year. We have available work Nationwide in Metropolitan and Regional areas.

We are now looking to recruit an experienced and qualified IT Support Technician to join our dedicated service team working in various locations throughout Australia.

The Role
We are looking for technically skilled candidate with good problem-solving ability for the position of IT Support Technician. The duties include being a reference point for all IT related queries at the user level, responding to user needs in a timely manner and ensuring the optimal running of all systems, among other technical duties.

The role includes but is not limited to the following duties:
Installing and configuring hardware and software components to ensure usability
Diagnosing, troubleshooting, and resolving connectivity, hardware, and software issues
Performing tests and evaluations of new software and hardware
Scheduling and conducting quality audit inspections, and analysing and reviewing systems, data and documentation
Identifying variations and potential high-risk areas in securing adherence to standards and procedures
Recommending corrective action plans and improvements in the resolution of non- compliance with standards detected through monitoring and auditing of processes and procedures
Communicating, educating, and liaising with users and management to ensure awareness and adherence to standards, procedures and quality control issues and activities
Assisting in troubleshooting, diagnosing, testing and resolving system problems and issues
Developing, conducting, and offering technical guidance and training in application software and operational procedures
Analysing, evaluating, and diagnosing technical problems and issues such as installation, maintenance, repair, upgrade and configuration and troubleshooting of desktops, software, hardware, printers, Internet, email, databases, operating systems and security systems
Testing, identifying and diagnosing functionality errors and faults in systems, and programming code within established testing protocols, guidelines and quality standards to ensure systems perform to specification
Performing organisational systems architecture reviews and assessments, and recommending current and future hardware and software strategies and directions
Creating and reviewing technical documentation such as procedural, instructional and operational guides and manuals, technical reports and specifications and maintenance inventory systems
Using project management methodologies, principles, and techniques to develop project plans and to cost, resource and manage projects
Test plans, which ensure acceptable quality and integrity of the system
Creating user and training documentation, and conducting formal training classes
Establishing good relationships with all departments and colleagues
Working with users to formulate and document business requirement
Investigating, and analysing business processes, procedures and work practices

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Previous work experience in the same field
3+ years of experience in computer networks and systems maintenance
Proficiency in computer systems, software installation, database programming, and cybersecurity basics
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Good interpersonal skills
Strong problem-solving, and time management skills
Attention to detail
Self-motivated and eager to learn and grow within the organisation

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

Who we are

Johnson Winter Slattery is a full service commercial firm with specialist expertise in all facets of commercial activity, covering the spectrum of transactional needs, advisory and compliance as well as dispute resolution.

Our lawyers and practice groups are ranked as leading, by Chambers Asia-Pacific, Asia Pacific Legal 500, Best Lawyers and Doyle’s Guide. We enjoy a reputation as a leading independent Australian firm focused on complex transactions and disputes.

We have over 500 professionals and support staff working in our Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Perth, Canberra and Brisbane offices.


About the Team

Our national IT support team provide timely and effective IT support to all JWS staff nationally. As the firm continues to grow and implement new technology to support the growth, our IT team manage all aspects of deployment to ensure a smooth and efficient user experience.
 

About the Role

An opportunity for an IT Support Officer exists to join our Sydney office on a full time basis. You will support the IT team to provide remote 1st level IT support to all members of the firm. In addition, you will provide 2nd level desktop support to members of our Sydney office.

This role will see you draw on your strong communication and customer service skills to troubleshoot or escalate day to day IT issues across the firm.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Hardware and software support, equipment set ups, and meeting room conference support
- ITIL service management process
- Service desk ticketing system call logging, and updating in accordance with SLA's
- Assist with IT changes and upgrades as directed

Our Sydney office is a welcoming and collaborative office that fosters a supportive and high-performing environment. This is an exciting opportunity to join a cohesive IT Support team.
 

About You

You obviously have plenty of technical aptitude and previous relevant experience, but there is much more to you. You:

- have a minimum of 1 yr previous experience with Microsoft OS and Office application support;
- operational knowledge of Microsoft Desktop technologies;
- familiarity with computer hardware and network technologies;
- excellent skills in critical thinking, problem solving, troubleshooting and analysis;
- work well under pressure, meet your deadlines and excel working in a team;
- have strong communication and stakeholder management skills and you aren't afraid to use them, internally and externally; and
- take a collaborative, positive and energetic approach to everything you do
- law firm or professional services experience is ideal
 

Working at JWS

We value collaboration and our teams work together to achieve shared outcomes. We care about the wellbeing of our people and will invest time in understanding your objectives so we can support you throughout your career. We believe it’s this focus on our people that has seen our firm grow rapidly to become one of Australia’s leading independent law firms.

We pride ourselves on being down-to-earth, approachable, and always high-performing. We have
worked hard to create a culture where people look out for each other.

We offer:

- A collegiate environment with a collaborative culture across offices and practice groups
- High-quality work with committed mentors supporting your career development
- Comprehensive benefits including competitive remuneration, flexible working, and extensive social and wellbeing initiatives
- Opportunities for professional growth through structured learning and development programs, and employee recognition initiatives
- Annual base salary of $79,900 plus superannuation

If you are looking for a challenging and rewarding opportunity to take your career to the next level, then we would love to hear from you.

Travel Agency Manager

Happy Travels is Australia’s leading backpacker travel agency, built on a passion for adventure and a commitment to creating unforgettable experiences. Despite the challenges faced by the travel industry in recent years, we’ve continued to grow by staying focused on what matters most - our people and our travellers.

We’re more than just a booking service. We’re a tight-knit, energetic team dedicated to helping backpackers and tourists make the most of their time in Australia, Fiji, and New Zealand. From once-in-a-lifetime tours to hidden local gems, we connect travellers with experiences that turn trips into lifelong memories.

At Happy Travels, it’s all about people, connection, and adventure.

Role Overview:

As a Travel Agency Manager, your primary focus will be to oversee the operations of our travel agency, ensuring exceptional service delivery and maximising sales performance. You will lead a team of Travel Sales Consultants, motivating and guiding them to achieve sales targets and provide outstanding customer experiences. A crucial part of your role will be the recruitment, training, and development of staff, ensuring they are equipped with the skills and knowledge to excel in their roles.

Key Responsibilities:
- Leading and overseeing the overall operations and strategic direction of the travel agency.
- Developing and implementing business plans and strategies to achieve company objectives and targets.
- Managing financial aspects, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial performance analysis.
- Building and maintaining relationships with key stakeholders, such as travel suppliers, partners, and clients.

Paediatric Basic Trainee

NSW Paediatric Physician Training Networks (Western, Northern, Eastern)

Paediatric Basic Training positions are accredited for basic training in General Paediatrics or Subspecialty training as outlined by the Royal Australasian College of Physicians. These positions are attached to one of the NSW Paediatric Physician Training Networks (i.e. Western, Northern, or Eastern), each which is made up of a number of health care facilities. As these are network positions, they involve training in a variety of locations and clinical departments. Duties will be performed at more than one place of work. To comply with Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP) training program requirements, trainees may be required to work in accredited facilities (including private hospitals). Facilities may be outside of NSW. The composition of each training network is provided in the attached document. There may be additional accredited facilities not listed. 

This position is open to all applicants and is also targeted for Aboriginal and - or Torres Strait Islander people. Aboriginal and - or Torres Strait Islander people are encouraged to apply and greater consideration will be given to suitable Aboriginal - Torres Strait Islander applicants, in order to improve access to employment and career opportunities. Exemption is claimed under Section 21 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977, NSW. If applying as an Australian Aboriginal- Torres Strait Islander, please include some information about your Aboriginal Australian - Torres Strait Islander identity in the cover letter of your application. If offered an interview, you can expand on this information at the interview itself in response to questions. 

** Trainees who have less than 12 months accredited paediatric training (at commencement of contract) in an accredited paediatric training program should apply for the Paediatric Physician Basic Trainee position - CAM30168**

**Trainees who have successfully passed the clinical exams in 2026 and have 6 months or less of basic training to complete all BT requirements in 2027 (i.e. all BT requirements will be finished at the end of Term 2 - 2027) should apply for an Advanced Trainee position - CAM30170**

Trainees complete Basic Training over three years (36 months full time equivalent) guided by the Basic Training handbooks and curricula in Paediatrics & Child Health. Physicians and other health professionals supervise and mentor trainees throughout their training. The Divisional Written Examination and Divisional Clinical Examination is towards the end of training to test a trainee's knowledge and skills and determine if they are eligible to progress to Advanced Training.

Positions are up to fulltime commencing from 01 February 2027. A limited number of job share opportunities may be considered within a network. Please refer to the position description, information document and contact person for further information about the position.

Interviews will be conducted virtually via videoconference in the week commencing Monday 10 August 2026.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Selection Criteria:

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia in an appropriate registration category.

Minimum of two years postgraduate experience, minimum 12 months recent accredited paediatric training and registered with the RACP (or equivalent) as a Basic Trainee, demonstrating progression through training.

Ongoing commitment to further education and professional development. This includes demonstrated ability to teach and willingness to participate in the teaching of Medical Students, Junior Medical Staff and other clinical staff. Please provide an example.

Demonstrated ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team to ensure the appropriate management of the patient. Please provide an example.

Demonstrated experience in taking comprehensive patient histories, performing clinical examinations and accurately documenting in patient records. Please provide an example.

Ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment. Please provide an example.

Demonstrated clinical competency in procedures in paediatric environments including venepuncture, intravenous cannulation, and neonatal resuscitation. Please provide an example.

Proven ability to organise, plan and manage competing tasks. Please provide an example.

Your application must include a current resume and responses to the application questions and criteria in the online application form. At Mushroom People Pty Ltd, we are a proud family-owned and operated gourmet mushroom farm located on the west side of Melbourne. Our deep passion for seeing mushrooms grow and staying connected to nature is at the heart of everything we do. We believe in sustainable, environmentally friendly farming practices that look after our local community and promote a healthier planet. Every single one of our gourmet varieties (including exotic Oyster and Lion's Mane varieties) is grown with love and delivered fresh to restaurants, grocery stores, and wholesalers across Australia.

As we expand our production, we are looking for a dedicated full-time Horticultural Grower (Mushroom Grower) (working 38 hours per week) to join our tight-knit farm family and help us grow with love.

The base salary offered is 79,500 - 82,500 per annum plus superannuation.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

- Planning and coordinating the cultivation, production, and marketing of gourmet mushroom crops from initial substrate preparation to final harvest, taking into careful account environmental variables and shifting market factors.
- Selecting, preparing, and inoculating grain spawn and liquid cultures, while grafting and testing new exotic mushroom strains to optimize crop resilience and yield.
- Maintaining optimal indoor crop production cycles by cultivating mycelium blocks, de-budding excess pinheads, monitoring flushing intervals, and adjusting climate control infrastructure.
- Organising and conducting daily commercial farming operations, including the strategic collecting, cold storage, strict grading, and eco-friendly packaging of fresh gourmet produce.
- Directing the sale, purchase, and dispatch of mushroom products to local wholesalers, restaurants, and grocery networks to meet tight delivery contracts.
- Overseeing general bio-secure farming activities, with a strict focus on non-chemical pest management, pathogen controls, and rigorous environmental hygiene.
- Maintaining facility infrastructure, specialised climate incubation rooms, commercial vertical shelf equipment, and automated water-misting supply systems.
- Evaluating comprehensive records of all farming activities, tracking market price fluctuations, and forecasting crop preparation volumes to meet seasonal consumer demand.
- Managing crop production within established budgets, tracking operational expenses, and reporting financial performance to business owners.
- Selecting, hiring, training, and supervising diverse farm staff and contractors to ensure total alignment with the farm's sustainable, family-oriented operational ethos.
- Overseeing climate and humidity controls within the grow rooms to protect crops from external weather fluctuations and ensure stable, year-round yields.
- Managing strict workplace health and safety (WHS) processes, while ensuring continuous facility compliance with Freshcare and HARPS food safety standards for exotic mushroom production.

Skills, Qualifications and Experience Required

- At least an AQF Certificate III or IV in Horticulture, Agriculture, or Agribusiness (Alternatively, at least 5 years of relevant work experience may be substituted for the degree).
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience in a supervisory or management role within an intensive primary production, commercial horticultural, or indoor cultivation environment.
- Strong knowledge and practical experience in agricultural production principles, specifically including indoor climate control, substrate handling, and crop hygiene.
- Demonstrated experience working within commercial food safety frameworks, with exposure to Freshcare and HARPS compliance and audit readiness highly regarded.
- Excellent communication, team leadership, and organisational skills, with a proven ability to manage daily tasks, lead a small production team, and meet strict harvesting and delivery deadlines.

The Role 

We are looking for an experienced and energetic Full-time Store Manager to join the team at our Brookvale store! As a Store Manager, you will be responsible for effectively managing all aspects of store operations, whilst building, leading, and driving a high performing team, to ensure delivery on business objectives and key performance indicators. You will be required to lead, coach and motivate the team, recruit and retain talent, and ensure operational excellence within your store. You will work to maintain the success of City Beach as an Australian retailer, ensuring positive and meaningful customer and people experiences throughout our retail network. 

This is a full-time position working an average of 38 hours per week.

Create a customer-centric culture by creating a supportive, development-focused environment that delivers exceptional people and customer experiences. 
Lead the store team to achieve KPI’s and operational efficiencies by setting clear expectations and managing performance across Sales, People, Compliance, Visual Merchandising, Wages, and Safety. 
Oversee daily store operations, including team leadership, stock management, loss prevention, store presentation, and promotional set-up.

Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, Port Lincoln Health Services 

Salary: WHD3 $1,250.29 to $1,281.40 per week + 12% Superannuation + Salary Sacrifice Benefits + Leave loading 

Permanent Full time position, working over a 7 day roster

Begin Your Journey as an Orderly at Eyre and Far North Local Health Network!

Port Lincoln Hospital is the region's principal healthcare facility, serving the Eyre Peninsula community with a broad range of acute and primary health services. If you take pride in practical, hands-on work and want it to genuinely matter to the people around you, this full-time ongoing role as a Service Assistant Orderly is worth your attention.

What You'll Be Doing

Working across Port Lincoln Hospital as part of the Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, you'll keep essential services moving so that clinical teams can focus on patient care. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Transporting patients safely and respectfully within the hospital

Collecting, delivering, and returning equipment to the correct areas

Transporting pathology and other specimens in line with handling protocols

Managing the delivery of clean linen and timely removal of soiled linen and waste

What You'll Bring

A reliable, punctual approach and the physical capacity to perform manual handling tasks throughout a full shift

Clear, respectful communication with patients, visitors, and healthcare staff

An understanding of, or willingness to learn, infection control and safe waste-handling procedures as required within SA Health facilities

The ability to prioritise competing tasks calmly in a busy hospital environment

Why Port Lincoln Hospital

As part of SA Health and the Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, you'll have access to salary packaging benefits that can meaningfully increase your take-home pay - a genuine advantage of working in the public health sector. Port Lincoln offers an enviable lifestyle on the Eyre Peninsula, with outstanding fishing, seafood, and open coastline right on the doorstep. The hospital team is close-knit, and the work you do each day has a direct, visible impact on patients and families who rely on local care. Ongoing employment means genuine job security, with the support and structure of one of South Australia's largest health employers behind you.

Ready to Apply?

Submit your application through the SA Health careers portal. Include a current resume and a brief cover letter outlining your suitability for the role. For questions about the position, reach out to the hiring manager - their details are listed in the role profile.

About Us 

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia's best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

The Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN) is responsible for the planning and delivery of hospital and health services over 337,626 square kilometres, taking in the Eyre Peninsula, western part of South Australia and north to Coober Pedy. We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

Click here to learn more about living and working in Eyre and Far North Local Health Network.

Why Join Us

Make a real difference and feel like an important part of the community. Being part of Eyre & Far North means you will be supported both personally and professionally, can take advantage of education and training opportunities, will have access to flexible working hours and be part of an inter-professional approach to holistic health care.

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information

Wellbeing and counselling support: support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program

Relocation support: relocation reimbursement of up to $15,000 may be available to people relocating for this opportunity. More information available from SA Health Careers - Relocation support.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Nautilus Aviation (as part of Morris Aviation) is a proven helicopter specialist with over 25 years flying experience and has grown to become one of Australia’s premier helicopter operators. Today our network of bases spans Cairns, Port Douglas, Townsville, Darwin, Jabiru, Gove and Torres Strait (Horn Island).

Nautilus Aviation has recently expanded its operations into southern Australia with the acquisition of Heli Surveys (including Snowy Mountains Helicopters), based in Jindabyne NSW in the heart of the Snowy Mountains.

We are now seeking a Senior Base Engineer to lead the maintenance operations at the Heli Surveys home base in Jindabyne.

This is an outstanding opportunity for a suitably qualified Licensed Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (LAME) with extensive helicopter experience who is looking for a rewarding career combined with an exceptional outdoor lifestyle.

We have a full-time position available for a highly experienced LAME. There is a variety of roster types and flexibility available for negotiation. As part of the role, you may be required to undertake short duration trips to alternate bases in support of our dynamic and varied fleet (including the Heli Surveys remote bases in Lakes Entrance, Victoria and Victor Harbor, South Australia).

As the Senior Base Engineer (LAME) for Heli Surveys as part of Nautilus Aviation, you will be responsible for ensuring aircraft are maintained to the highest standards of safety and airworthiness while working closely with our Chief Engineer and Head of Airworthiness & Maintenance Control (HAAMC), based in North Queensland.

The Senior Base Engineer (LAME) will be charged with:

-  Overseeing all maintenance and servicing on the fleet of AS350/H125, Bell 407, Bell 212 and Bell 412 helicopters
-  Certifying for line and heavy maintenance on the fleet of AS350/H125, Bell 407, Bell 212 and Bell 412 helicopters both at home base and in remote locations when required
-  Certifying for defect rectifications / rectifying breakdowns on our AS350/H125, Bell 407, Bell 212 and Bell 412 fleet both at home base and at remote locations as required
-  Leading and supervising all other LAME's, AME's and Apprentices on a day to day basis in carrying out maintenance on company aircraft

-  Communicating with the company Chief Engineer and Head of Airworthiness & Maintenance Control (HAAMC) and operations to ensure all stakeholders are informed of current status of all aircraft

Working as a Licensed Aircraft Maintenance Engineer for Heli Surveys and Morris Group will include:

-  Relocation assistance to the right candidate
-  Competitive remuneration package
-  Opportunity to work across a diverse fleet of helicopters
-  Work on a varied range of rotary wing aircraft

-  Winter ski season pass
-  Summer mountain biking season pass
-  Exclusive employee discounts across the Morris Group's hospitality, tourism and leisure businesses
-  Career development opportunities across Heli Surveys, Nautilus Aviation and the wider Morris Group

REQUIREMENTS:

To be successful in this role as a Licensed Aircraft Maintenance Engineer, you must have:

-  The right to live and work in Australia (visa sponsorship may be considered for the right candidate)
-  Valid Australian Driver’s license
-  CASA-recognised Aircraft Maintenance Engineer qualifications
-  CASA recognised qualifications/licence : B412 and/or B212
-  Experience maintaining AS350/H125 helicopters
-  Experience maintaining Bell helicopters
-  Leadership and management skills
-  Ability to lead a team of LAME's, AME's, Apprentices and other staff
-  Excellent verbal and written communication skills
-  Computer literacy with experience on aircraft computer aided maintenance systems
-  Strong organisational skills
-  The ability to prioritise workloads and manage competing demands
-  The ability to work both independently and as part of a team
-  A proactive, self-motivated approach
-  A strong commitment to a safe work environment and legal/regulatory compliance
-  Positive and professional attitude
-  Current ASIC and Human Factors qualifications (or ability to obtain/renew with company assistance)

Desirable:

-  Preference will be given to candidates with experience in AS350/H125, Bell 407, Bell 212/412 and Robinson R44 helicopters
-  Experience with other helicopters including EC130, 505, Bell 407 / 206L / 206A/B
-  Experience using Computer Maintenance and Management Systems – Aerotrack MRO(Aust) and Air Maestro will be an advantage
-  Forklift ticket

ABOUT US:

With more than 25 years of operational experience, Heli Surveys has established itself as one of Australia's leading utility helicopter operators. As part of the Morris Group and sister company to Nautilus Aviation, we operate from a network of bases including Cairns, Port Douglas, Townsville, Darwin, Jabiru, Gove, Horn Island and Jindabyne.

Our fleet supports a wide variety of utility operations throughout Australia, providing our engineers with diverse and interesting work in a dynamic environment.

Nautilus Aviation has built an outstanding reputation based on the quality and diversity of our fleet of helicopters and our commitment to the safety of all passengers and personnel at all times.

We pride ourselves on our customer service from the delivery of commercial air work, pilot training, Search & Rescue and chartered flights all while working in partnership with a number of top tourism operators to deliver leisure experiences over some of the iconic natural landscapes of Australia.

Nautilus Aviation and Heli Surveys are part of the Morris Group of companies. Morris Group is an independent, family-run business that was founded in 1980 and operates a collection of iconic Australian experiences. With businesses in tourism, hospitality, aviation, and technology, we’re on a mission to make a positive impact doing work we love. From luxury resorts and lodges to urban beer gardens, elevated dining experiences, and super-yacht adventures; everything we do is inspired by our love for good company and the great outdoors.

In addition to Nautilus Aviation, Morris Group also owns and operates a collection of hotels and luxury lodges in Queensland as part of Morris Escapes – including Beechmont Estate, Orpheus Island Lodge, Pelorus Island and Mt Mulligan Lodge. Morris Group is also the owner of the world-class holiday destinations The Ville Resort-Casino and Ardo Hotel, both located in Townsville QLD.

Morris Group also includes Morris Hospitality that focuses on creating elevated dining experiences with venues including the Albert Park Hotel, Portsea Hotel, Railway Club Hotel, O’Connell’s, Half Moon and the Lucky Coq in Victoria, the Julatten Hotel in Queensland and CBCo Brewing in Victoria and Western Australia.

If you excel at delivering world class service and have experience as a Licensed Aircraft Maintenance Engineer, we want to hear from you!

Location: Nightcliff NT 0810
Employment Type: Full-time
Salary: AUD $90,000 – $110,000 plus superannuation

About us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the business
The business (ABN 24 638 483 600) is a locally owned real estate agency in Darwin, Northern Territory, servicing Darwin and Palmerston. They provide real estate sales, rental, property management and client-focused real estate services. They are seeking an experienced Sales and Marketing Manager to lead agency growth, sales strategy, marketing campaigns and client acquisition.

About the Role
The Sales and Marketing Manager will plan, direct and coordinate the agency’s sales and marketing activities. The role will focus on growing property listings, improving brand visibility, developing client acquisition strategies and supporting the agency’s long-term business growth in the Darwin and Palmerston property markets.

Duties and Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
- Developing and implementing sales and marketing strategies for the agency.
- Leading campaigns to attract property sellers, buyers, landlords and tenants.
- Setting sales targets, marketing objectives and business development plans.
- Managing marketing budgets, campaign priorities and promotional activities.
- Reviewing market trends, local property data and competitor activity.
- Developing strategies to grow the agency’s property management portfolio and sales listings.
- Managing brand positioning, client engagement and digital marketing direction.
- Coordinating advertising campaigns for properties and agency services.
- Supporting and guiding staff involved in sales, marketing, leasing and client engagement.
- Building relationships with clients, referral partners, contractors and community networks.
- Monitoring campaign performance, enquiry conversion and business development outcomes.
- Preparing management reports and recommendations for business growth.

Skills and Experience Required
Applicants must have:
- A bachelor degree or higher qualification in business, marketing, management or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
- At least 3 years of experience in sales, marketing, business development or management.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement sales and marketing strategies.
- Strong leadership, communication and negotiation skills.
- Experience managing campaigns, budgets, performance targets and client relationships.
- Strong understanding of digital marketing, lead generation and customer engagement.
- Experience in real estate, property services or professional services will be highly regarded.
- Ability to analyse market trends and use data to support strategic decisions.
- Current driver licence is desirable.

How to Apply
We are looking for professionals who are passionate about real estate and can demonstrate their experience clearly and confidently.
To apply, submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
- A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a dynamic real estate team and contributing to exceptional property and client experiences, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 20 August 2026

Bevelling experience
Multi-torch and plasm and oxy cutting experience
Able to work productively, largely unsupervised
Willing to operate new equipment
Knowledge and expertise with steel
Excellent problem solving and reasoning abilities
Reliable, self-motivated with a great work ethic
A self-starter, with an ability to take direction
Excellent problem solver and reasoning abilities
Take pride in your work and your station
Operate forklift (desired but not essential)
A strong team player

The successful applicant will be joining a secure, reputable organisation who offers their employees opportunities for career progression.
If you have the skills & experience we need and have a positive attitude, please apply now.

Note: Only short-listed candidates will be contacted. We promote a safe work culture; therefore, we have a process of reference checking and pre-employment medicals which includes a drug and alcohol screen for the successful applicant.

Exciting Casual Opportunity: Community Support Worker 

In the remote communities of Cleve, Cowell, and Kimba, a Community Support Worker does more than complete a checklist - you help someone stay in the home they love, on their own terms. At Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN), your presence in Eastern Eyre is the thread that connects clients to their independence, their community, and the life they've built.

Your Role in the Community

Working within EFNLHN's Consumer Directed Care model, you'll deliver support shaped by each client's own goals and preferences. No two days are identical, and that's by design. Key responsibilities include:

Assisting clients with personal hygiene, grooming, and mobility with respect and dignity

Performing household tasks including cleaning, laundry, meal preparation, and minor gardening

Providing reliable transport to appointments and community outings

Supporting social engagement and activities that contribute to client wellbeing

At the WHA4 level, delivering personal care to clients with more complex support needs

A warm, empathetic approach and the confidence to work independently across small remote communities

Sound communication skills and genuine respect for people from diverse cultures and backgrounds

Experience supporting aged, frail, or disabled individuals in a home or community setting

We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

Make a real difference and feel like an important part of the community. Being part of Eyre & Far North means you will be supported both personally and professionally, can take advantage of education and training opportunities, will have access to flexible working hours and be part of an inter-professional approach to holistic health care.

 Apply now
 Job no: 944342

 Work type: Full time

 Location: Yorke and Mid North

 Categories: Community and Social Services, Child, Aged and Disability Care, Nursing-Midwifery





 

Yorke and Northern Local Health Network, Riverton Hospital

Registered and Enrolled Nurses

Salary: $77,824 to $106,187 p.a. (pro rata) RN-M1 | $66,552 - $77,824 p.a. (pro rata) ENC-END

Eligibility Open to Everyone 

Riverton Hospital - where care feels personal and careers feel meaningful

Registered Nurse 

Permanent 3.33FTE

Enrolled Nurse

Permanent 0.84FTE

WHERE YOU'LL BE AND WHAT YOU'LL DO

Riverton Hospital has 7 acute beds and 17 RAC aged care beds. We are a small, yet dynamic hospital servicing the local town and surrounding communities. Linked onsite with the local GP clinic, you will be exposed to a variety of patient presentations from emergency retrieval, low priority attendances, palliation, long term aged care, and everything in between - there is something for everyone at Riverton Hospital!

Set in the beautiful country town of Riverton, South Australia, 89km from Adelaide CBD. As a nurse you will fulfill a role that is engaging, fulfilling and a valued part of the country community.

Riverton is a friendly, peaceful, and scenically beautiful town, nested in the rolling hills just north of Roseworthy and not far from the renowned Clare Valley. With local schools, shops, and services there is everything you might need on hand, and if not, it's not a far drive to other nearby centres.

Our hospital and aged care facility thrive on a positive culture, where staff are valued and recognised as significant contributors to the ongoing health and wellbeing of the community we care for. We value everyone's skills, experience and contribution and emphasise a positive mindset aiming to bring our best to our work every day. You will be part of a team that works together, to support each other and provide the best service we can for our patients and our residents. We are proud of our facility and proud to be a part of the community of Riverton - come and join us!

Role Overview

Your role as a nurse will be varied, exciting, and full of opportunity! Given we are a country hospital, our nurses are known for being able to manage whatever comes through our doors, whether it is a critical event or a low priority attendance. You will develop and maintain your skills in triage, acute emergency, mental health, palliation and so much more. In addition, our attached residential aged care facility will offer you a solid nursing foundation in the ongoing management of the care of our valued residents and the challenges and accomplishment that working in aged care can bring.

There will also be opportunity to take on additional portfolios such as blood management, palliative care, education of students, work health and safety, infection control and many others. We offer extensive education opportunities to all our nursing staff as well as opportunities for career advancement into specialist acute roles, education, management, and others. Wherever you want to head with your nursing career, we can help you get there in the Yorke and Northern Local Health Network.

WHO ARE WE AND WHAT WE OFFER?

The Yorke and Northern Local Health Network (YNLHN) supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe in their work environment encouraging all people to use their talents and be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

A career in the YNLHN can be very rewarding and comes with great lifestyles benefits. Not to mention your choice of scenery from farm to ocean, vineyards, and the Southern Flinders Ranges.

About the Role:

Modbury Hospital's Emergency Department is a busy, community-facing service at the heart of Adelaide's northern suburbs - and the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is looking for a Registered Nurse or Clinical Nurse to join the team on a part-time, ongoing basis.

Your Role in the Department as a Registered Nurse

Working across a diverse ED caseload, you'll deliver evidence-based nursing care to patients across the acuity spectrum - from triage through to discharge or admission. Key responsibilities include:

Assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating patient care in line with NALHN clinical standards

Triaging patients using the Australasian Triage Scale and escalating deteriorating patients through recognised response pathways

Collaborating with a multidisciplinary team to support safe, timely patient flow through the department

Contributing to a learning environment by supporting students and less-experienced colleagues in clinical practice

Your Role in the Department as a Clinical Nurse

Accepts accountability for their own practice standards, activities delegated to others and the guidance and development of less experienced staff.

The Clinical Nurse role at this level continues to be predominantly clinical in nature; however employees are assigned appropriate portfolios. The allocation of portfolio responsibilities should be negotiated with each employee and be consistent with the career development plan for the employee as determined by their performance review-development plan.

What You'll Bring

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (AHPRA)

Demonstrated emergency or acute care nursing experience in a hospital setting

Sound clinical assessment skills and working knowledge of deteriorating patient management

Strong communication skills across patients, families, and multidisciplinary teams

Commitment to the SA Health Care Act requirements, including a satisfactory Department for Human Services screening

Ability to work rotating shifts, including nights and weekends, consistent with SA Health enterprise agreement conditions

To be eligible for this position, you must be Registered or eligible for registration as a Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and who holds, or who is eligible to hold, a current practicing certificate

About Adelaide:

About Us:

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management.

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community.

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services:

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services.

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services.

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care.

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings.

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites.

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains.

Salary packaging is an option for saving money by paying for some of your everyday expenses from your salary before it is taxed.

Relocation assistance may be available for successful applicants from interstate or overseas.

NALHN supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if you have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.
